note: Re-judged 2026-11-02 by an independent auditor who authored none of the bgp-role changes. RFC 9234 Section 4.1: "An eBGP speaker MUST NOT advertise multiple versions of the BGP Role Capability." The only change to the file-scoped .ci units it judged (655d07b59b, 3459b6e390) deletes the `policy { reject-asn NO-TRANSIT { indirect [ 3356 ] } }` block, its four comment lines, and `filters [ inactive:NO-TRANSIT ];` from each bound import and export chain, leaving `final accept;`. That filter was deactivated and never ran; it existed only because the config then required a role's bound chain to name a transit-refusing filter, and 655d07b59b made that check a filter the bgp-role plugin inserts itself. Every OPEN capability option, every action=send and every expect/reject line (the exact NOTIFICATION or UPDATE hex) is byte-identical, so each case still isolates the same condition and asserts the same exact outcome. Verdict unchanged: enforced. Earlier judgement follows. Rejudged 2026-10-31 by an auditor who authored none of the change. The only change to test/plugin/dynamic-peer-gets-group-role-capability.ci since the last stamp is cabb706c11 moving the policy block from inside bgp {} to the top-level policy root, the same lines re-indented; every action, expect, reject and option line is byte-identical, so the carriers drive the same inputs and assert the same outcomes. Verdict unchanged. RFC 9234 Section 4.1: "An eBGP speaker MUST NOT advertise multiple versions of the BGP Role Capability." The single-polarity annotation remains justified: config.go::parseRoleContainer reads one scalar import role and extractRoleCapabilities emits one declaration per selected peer; reactor/peer.go::getPluginCapabilities consumes those declarations for its selector set. TestExtractRoleCapabilities_ParseBGPConfig requires exactly one capability and one peer for every configured role. dynamic-peer-gets-group-role-capability.ci asserts the whole OPEN with exactly one 090101 TLV, including all enclosing lengths; duplicate emission cannot hide behind a substring assertion. No fabricated negative configuration is required. Rejudged independently against RFC source and every tagged carrier on 2026-10-22. Functional judgments use the corresponding test/draft/plugin files, not the unpromoted old-syntax live files. Their inactive NO-TRANSIT import/export policies explicitly end in accept; reactor runEgressPolicyChain applies that final only after mandatory in-process OTC, and OPEN validation is independent. This is a source judgment, not a new runtime or discrimination result; parent owns promotion and native freshness before stamping.
